subject: Orchid Health: Private deployment intake — acceptance matrix & ownership tollgates
messages:
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@orchidhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <pri@orchidhealth.com>, Orchid Health - Infra Team <infra@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partner intake: private deploy needs & initial artifacts

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to proceed. We want to evaluate a Private deployment (VPC peering OR on-prem bundle) for our production traffic. To speed things up, can you confirm what you need from us to get to a Day-0 smoke run? High level:

- Expected peak throughput: ~120 req/s, 1.6k tokens/minute average per instance.
- Data locality: deploy into our Azure VNet (preferred) but we can do on-prem if required.
- Key management: we use Azure Key Vault and need a KMS integration/rotation plan.
- Audit/compliance: SOC2 logs and retained request traces for 90 days.
- Network: public egress allowlist (we'll provide IPs) + required inbound peering ports.

Attached are a rough network diagram and our vendor security QA PDF. Please point us to an onboarding checklist and any ownership lanes — we want a crisp intake so internal and external teams know who owns what.

Attachments: orchid_network_diagram_v1.png, Orchid_Security_QA.pdf

Best,
Sam Wong
Director of Platform Engineering
Orchid Health
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Partner intake: private deploy needs & initial artifacts

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Orchid's intake. They gave peak numbers and attached network + QA. I sketched an acceptance matrix and a set of "tollgates" we should run the account through; please review and flag gaps.

Proposed onboarding tollgates (ownership lanes in parentheses):

1) Intake & SOW sign-off (Sales / Legal)
   - Confirm deployment mode: VNet peering (preferred) or on-prem bundle.
   - DocuSign SOW + billing terms.

2) Connectivity & Access (Infra / NetEng)
   - IP allowlist and peering config (Customer provides subnet / BGP info).
   - Service account + bastion/Jumpbox requirements, plus SSH keyflow.

3) Security Evidence & KMS (Security / App Sec)
   - KMS integration plan (Azure Key Vault mapping).
   - SOC2 artifact handoff and log retention SLA (90 days).
   - Customer-provided compliance questionnaire responses.

4) Day-0 Smoke & Performance (SRE / Runtime)
   - Smoke tests: token-level latency targets, KV cache sanity, KV eviction.
   - Load run to validate 120 req/s throughput.

5) Cutover & Post-cutover Ops (CS / Support)
   - Rollback plan, runbook, monitoring hooks (traces + cost telemetry).

Questions for you both:
- Who on our side will own the KMS integration? I'm proposing Marissa as lead, Ben as net/ops contact.
- Do we require a customer-managed bastion or can we supply ephemeral session tokens through our control plane?

Action: Marissa to produce a compact acceptance matrix (one-pager) we can send to Orchid with clear asks and three kickoff windows.

Thanks,
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wong <sam.wong@orchidhealth.com>, Priya Desai <pri@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner intake: private deploy needs & initial artifacts — acceptance matrix attached

Hi Sam / Priya,

Appreciate the quick context and the attachments. Attached is a concise "Acceptance matrix & ownership lanes" (orchid_mal_action_plan.xlsx) that maps each tollgate to specific deliverables, owners, and success criteria. Summary (high-level):

- Connectivity: we need the peering subnets, BGP ASN if applicable, and the three public egress IPs you plan to add to our allowlist. Success = established peering and traffic flows during smoke.
- KMS: mapping between your Azure Key Vault roles and our runtime key IDs. Success = ability to fetch/decrypt a test secret from your vault during Day-0 smoke.
- Compliance: a single PDF of your SOC2 artifact list + where logs are retained. Success = evidence uploaded to the shared Drive + acceptance by our security reviewer.
- Smoke tests: we will run a 15-minute throughput test at 120 req/s, and a latency SLA check. Success = 95th percentile within the agreed target.

Please review the attached matrix and confirm:
1) Preferred kickoff window (pick three): Sep 25 AM, Sep 26 PM, Sep 28 AM (PDT).
2) Who is our primary infra contact for network configs (name + email).
3) Do you want us to run with a customer-managed bastion or our ephemeral session approach? We recommend customer-managed bastion for regulated environments.

Attachments: orchid_mal_action_plan.xlsx

If everything looks ok I'll log the first tollgate in HubSpot and create the scoped DocuSign for the SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@orchidhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <pri@orchidhealth.com>, Orchid Health - Infra Team <infra@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partner intake: private deploy needs & initial artifacts — acceptance matrix attached

Marissa / David —

Thanks for the matrix. We confirm the Sep 25 AM window as preferred. Our infra lead is Priya Desai (pri@orchidhealth.com) and she'll be the single point for peering configs. We prefer a customer-managed bastion.

Quick answers:
- We'll share the three egress IPs and BGP details by EOD 9/20.
- SOC2 artifacts: we uploaded the index to your shared Drive link (see hubspot doc).
- KMS: Priya will link a service principal that your runtime can use to fetch test secrets.

Onward — looking forward to the kickoff. Attaching a slightly updated network diagram (orchid_network_diagram_v1.png).

— Sam
